subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic marker-controlled inbound continuation contract, treat existing debounce and collect modes as the supported answer, or route this through a plugin/API seam first?
rationale: The request adds new public config and changes how inbound fragments become a single agent turn, so automation cannot safely choose marker syntax, timeout, stripping, media, command, transcript, and typing semantics.

options.title: Design generic ingress continuation
options.body: Add one opt-in core or SDK-backed continuation contract with typed config, schema/docs, marker stripping, timeout behavior, and tests across inbound debounce, queue, transcript, and typing behavior.

options.title: Document existing batching as sufficient
options.body: Keep marker syntax out of core and explicitly steer users toward messages.inbound debounce and messages.queue.collect for cost-reduction batching.

options.title: Require plugin/API seam first
options.body: Defer the feature until a channel/plugin ingress extension point can implement marker buffering without growing core message config.

recommendation.title: Design generic ingress continuation
recommendation.body: Add one opt-in core or SDK-backed continuation contract with typed config, schema/docs, marker stripping, timeout behavior, and tests across inbound debounce, queue, transcript, and typing behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across the current inbound debounce policy, schema/config, queue drain, and prior product-review context.
